title: Quick check: Global Error Handling

questions.prompt: In the context of “Global Error Handling” and “global-error.js”, What does an App Router `loading.jsx` convention provide?
options: The answer key for an exam.
A route-segment loading UI, commonly connected to a Suspense boundary.
A security check that replaces route authorization.
questions.answer_key: A route-segment loading UI, commonly connected to a Suspense boundary.
questions.explanation: The loading convention supplies pending UI; it does not replace data validation or authorization.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Global Error Handling”, When should an application use not-found behavior?
options: When a requested resource or route does not exist or is intentionally unavailable as a not-found case.
For every temporary network error, regardless of meaning.
To tell a user that a mutation succeeded when it failed.
To show internal environment variables to the user.
questions.answer_key: When a requested resource or route does not exist or is intentionally unavailable as a not-found case.
questions.explanation: A clear distinction among not-found, recoverable errors, and server errors helps users and monitoring.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Global Error Handling”, What belongs in a production error message?
options: Full stack traces and secret values.
A safe explanation and a recovery or retry path, while sensitive diagnostics stay in server logs.
The raw body of every rejected upstream response.
questions.answer_key: A safe explanation and a recovery or retry path, while sensitive diagnostics stay in server logs.
questions.explanation: Production experiences should aid recovery without disclosing internals.
